title: Lesson 1: Defining a routine
lessonSummary: Great! You wrote your first training routine and ran it several times.

tasks.instruction: Run this example: One routine is defined once and called twice.
tasks.codeTemplate:
def greet_horse():
    print("Hello, Stormwind!")
    print("Time for training!")

greet_horse()
greet_horse()

tasks.instruction: Define a function groom_horse() that prints exactly The coat shines! and call it three times.

validation.expected:
The coat shines!
The coat shines!
The coat shines!

tasks.instruction: Define a function feed() that prints exactly The horse eats hay. Call it once, then print exactly Done! (outside the function).

title: Lesson 2: One parameter
lessonSummary: Nice! Your routine can now do something different for every horse.

tasks.instruction: Run this example: The same routine greets two different horses.
Write a function praise_horse(name) that prints Well done, <name>! Call it with "Stormwind" and then with "Lightning".

validation.expected:
Well done, Stormwind!
Well done, Lightning!

tasks.instruction: Write a function show_age(age) that prints Age: <age> years Call it with the numbers 4 and 9 (without quotes).

title: Lesson 3: Several parameters
lessonSummary: Great! Your routines now take several ingredients in the right order.

tasks.instruction: Run this example: Three arguments fill three parameters – in the right order.
tasks.codeTemplate:
def introduce_horse(name, breed, age):
    print(f"Name: {name}")
    print(f"Breed: {breed}")
    print(f"Age: {age}")

introduce_horse("Stormwind", "Hanoverian", 6)

tasks.instruction: Write a function jump(obstacle, height) that prints Jump over <obstacle>: <height> cm Call it with ("Oxer", 120) and then with ("Water jump", 90).

validation.expected:
Jump over Oxer: 120 cm
Jump over Water jump: 90 cm

tasks.instruction: The function order_feed(kind, amount) is already finished. Call it so that it prints exactly Ordered: 5 kg oats Watch the order of the arguments!

title: Lesson 4: Returning values with return
lessonSummary: Nice! Your routines now deliver results you can keep calculating with.

tasks.instruction: Run this example: The result is stored and used right away.
tasks.codeTemplate:
def calculate_distance(laps, length):
    return laps * length

distance = calculate_distance(3, 200)
print(f"Distance: {distance} m")
print(f"Long lap: {calculate_distance(5, 400)} m")

tasks.instruction: Write a function double_oats(kilos) that returns kilos * 2 with return. Print exactly Double: 8 kg by using double_oats(4).
Write a function calculate_hoof_points(laps, points_per_lap) that returns laps * points_per_lap. Store calculate_hoof_points(4, 15) in the variable points and print exactly Hoof points: 60

title: Lesson 5: return or print?
lessonSummary: Well spotted! You now know when a routine prints and when it returns.

tasks.instruction: Run this example: A function without return gives back None.
tasks.codeTemplate:
def show_stable_plan():
    print("Box 1: Stormwind, Box 2: Luna")

result = show_stable_plan()
print(f"Return value: {result}")

tasks.instruction: The function calculate_oats calculates the need but does not return it – that is why it prints Oats: None. Add return so that exactly Oats: 18 is printed.
tasks.codeTemplate:
def calculate_oats(horses, kilos):
    total = horses * kilos

oats = calculate_oats(6, 3)
print(f"Oats: {oats}")

tasks.instruction: Write a function total_price(price, amount) that returns price * amount. Use it: total = total_price(25, 4), money = 150 - total. Print exactly Money left: 50

title: Lesson 6: Decisions and loops in functions
lessonSummary: Masterful! Your routines can now decide and repeat.

tasks.instruction: Run this example: The function returns a different text depending on the speed.
Write a function is_ready(fitness) that returns True if fitness is at least 70, otherwise False. Print is_ready(80) and then is_ready(50) with print.

Write a function count_jumps(laps) that adds all numbers from 1 to laps with a for loop (lap 1 has 1 jump, lap 2 has two jumps, …) and returns the sum. Print exactly Jumps: 55 by using count_jumps(10).

title: Lesson 7: Docstrings and good names
lessonSummary: Excellent! Your routines now have descriptions and good names.

tasks.instruction: Run this example: The docstring is shown with __doc__.
tasks.codeTemplate:
def calculate_feed(horses):
    """Calculates the daily amount of feed."""
    return horses * 8

print(calculate_feed.__doc__)
print(calculate_feed(5))

validation.expected: Calculates the daily amount of feed.

tasks.instruction: Write a function show_stable_rule() with the docstring "Shows the most important stable rule." (in triple quotes) that prints Always close the door! First print show_stable_rule.__doc__, then call the function.

validation.expected:
Shows the most important stable rule.
Always close the door!

tasks.instruction: The function is called ar(l, w) – a bad name. Rename it to calculate_area(length, width) (also the parameters in the body) so the call below works and prints exactly Area: 21

result = calculate_points

title: Mission 1: The Stable Apprentice
lessonSummary: The Stable Apprentice is trained: You wrote routines, called them and delivered results!

tasks.instruction: Step 1 – Greeting: Write a function greet_stable() that prints exactly Welcome to the stable! Call it twice.

validation.expected:
Welcome to the stable!
Welcome to the stable!

tasks.instruction: Step 2 – Calculate feed: Write a function calculate_feed(horses, kilos) that returns horses * kilos. Print exactly Feed: 24 kg by using calculate_feed(8, 3).

Step 3 – Room free? Write a function has_room(boxes, horses) that returns True if boxes is at least horses, otherwise False. Print Barn: True (12 boxes, 10 horses) and then Pasture: False (5 boxes, 8 horses).

title: Mission 2: The Tournament Planner
lessonSummary: The Tournament Planner stands: Your functions now build complete start cards!

tasks.instruction: Step 1 – Points: Write a function calculate_points(jumps, faults) that returns jumps * 10 - faults * 5. Print exactly Points: 70 by using calculate_points(8, 2).
Step 2 – Start number: Write a function create_start_number(name, number) that returns the text <number>: <name> Print exactly 7: Stormwind by printing create_start_number("Stormwind", 7).

Step 3 – Start card: The functions from steps 1 and 2 are provided. Write show_start_card(name, number, jumps, faults) that prints three lines: the start number, Points: <points> and Faults: <faults> Call it with ("Stormwind", 7, 8, 2).

title: Mission 3: The Training Planner
lessonSummary: The Training Planner runs: Duration, fitness check and display work hand in hand!

tasks.instruction: Step 1 – Duration: Write a function calculate_duration(laps) that returns laps * 5 (minutes). Print exactly Duration: 40 minutes by using calculate_duration(8).

Step 2 – Trainable? Write a function can_train(fitness, duration) that returns True if fitness is at least duration * 2, otherwise False. Print Stormwind: True (fitness 90, duration 40) and then Lightning: False (fitness 60, duration 40).

Step 3 – Training display: The two functions are provided. Write show_training(name, fitness, laps): It prints <name>: training <duration> minutes if the horse may train, otherwise <name>: needs a break. Call it with ("Stormwind", 90, 8) and ("Lightning", 60, 8).

validation.expected:
Stormwind: training 40 minutes
Lightning: needs a break

title: Extra Challenge 1: The Course Scoring
lessonSummary: The Course Scoring runs: Time bonus, total points and display fit together!

tasks.instruction: Step 1 – Time bonus: Write a function calculate_time_bonus(seconds): up to and including 60 seconds there are 20 bonus points, up to and including 90 seconds 10, otherwise 0. For 55, 80 and 100 seconds print Bonus: 20, Bonus: 10 and Bonus: 0 one after another.
Step 2 – Total points: calculate_time_bonus is provided. Write calculate_total(faults, seconds) that returns 100 - faults * 4 + time bonus. Print exactly Total: 108 by using calculate_total(3, 55).

Step 3 – Scoring: Both functions are provided. Write show_score(name, faults, seconds) that prints <name>: <total points> points, and call it in a for loop for "Stormwind" with 0, 1 and 2 faults (55 seconds each).

validation.expected:
Stormwind: 120 points
Stormwind: 116 points
Stormwind: 112 points

title: Extra Challenge 2: The Stable Manager
lessonSummary: The Stable Manager stands: Costs, budget and report work together!

tasks.instruction: Step 1 – Feed costs: Write a function calculate_feed_costs(horses, days) that returns horses * days * 4. Print exactly Feed costs: 280 by using calculate_feed_costs(10, 7).

Step 2 – Is the money enough? Write a function is_money_enough(costs, money) that returns True if money is at least costs, otherwise False. Print Enough: True (costs 280, money 300) and then Enough: False (costs 280, money 200).

Step 3 – Report: Both functions are provided. Write barn_report(barn, horses, days, money) that prints three lines: Barn <barn>, Feed costs: <costs> and Enough: <True/False>. Call it with ("North", 10, 7, 300).

validation.expected:
Barn North
Feed costs: 280
Enough: True

title: Extra Challenge 3: The Big Race
lessonSummary: The Big Race runs: Speed, laps and result fit together!

tasks.instruction: Step 1 – Speed: Write a function calculate_speed(base, weight) that returns base - weight, but never less than 0. Print Speed: 25 (base 40, weight 15) and then Speed: 0 (base 10, weight 30).

Step 2 – Race lap: Write a function run_lap(distance, speed) that returns the new remaining distance (distance - speed, but never below 0). Start with distance = 100, call run_lap(distance, 25) twice (store the result in distance again) and print Distance: <distance> after each call.

Step 3 – Race: run_lap is provided. Write simulate_race(distance, speed, laps): A for loop (lap 1 to laps) calls run_lap each time and prints Lap <number>: <distance> m to go At the end the function returns the remaining distance. Call it with (100, 30, 4), store the result in left and print Left: <left>

validation.expected:
Lap 1: 70 m to go
Lap 2: 40 m to go
Lap 3: 10 m to go
Lap 4: 0 m to go
Left: 0
